Player Cheat Sheet: Core Flow

1) Core Roll

Attribute k MR: Roll Attribute d8, keep MR, sum the kept dice. Natural 8s explode (designated Critical: 7–8). Guaranteed Eight: trade 8 Pool dice for one exploding 8, counted as one result. Example: Might 8, MR 3 = 8k3.

2) Training Checks

Four freely named Professions at Rank 2, plus Perception Rank 2 free. Describe how your Profession fits the task; if none fits, try untrained. One universal Training Roll: Attribute k MR with the relevant Training Advantage (Rank 1: reroll 1; 2: 1-2; 3: 1-3; 4: 1-4; 5: 1-5; 6-8: 1-6, once per eligible initial die). Training Crit at Rank 7: once per Tyhran Day; Rank 8: twice per day, per Profession or Perception; declare before rolling, exploding on natural 7-8. Standard Check: against Task TN = 4 x Task Level; optional declared Raises add +4 TN each and grant feasible effects on success, with no Training Rank Raise cap. Comparative Check: both parties roll; higher wins, defending/observing side wins ties; no Task TN or Raises. Rank 0 uses Disadvantage and no Raises. Familiar safe work may succeed routinely.

Echo Imprints: Immediately after starting Attributes, choose up to MR free Imprints tied to Attributes 4+; they express small magic and Echo Memories.

3) Raises

Combat: Before an Attack or Casting Roll, declare the number of Paid Raises and commit the number of eligible Intellect Free Raises. Paid +4 TN; Free +0. After the roll and hit checks, choose the Damage/Special allocation for those Raises; never add more Raises after the roll. A successful Damage Raise grants +MR d8 (AoE: +ceil(MR/2) d8); a Special Raise adds +MR to an existing numeric Special. Special-only Attacks (Single Target or AoE) may use only Special Raises, never Damage Raises. AoE, Split Attack and Autofire choose one shared after-roll allocation per Power use. Persistent Special Zones and Special Auras cannot use Raises because they make no Attack or Casting Roll. Spells use Base TN = cast PL × 4; direct Spells add effective Spell Resistance and Paid Raises to the target's TN. Other placed Spells use their normal Creation TN.

Rituals: Every character knows all 16 Core Rituals. Stones are mandatory; no Profession is required. Explain the method and choose a fitting Attribute; spend 1 Tyhran Hour and Seal Stones. A learned Profession helps only when the player explains a credible connection and the GM approves it; then apply its Training Advantage and available Training Crit. Without one, use the full Attribute Pool with no mundane Untrained Disadvantage. Base TN = 4 x max(3, Task Level); 8 Raises maximum across named tier 0-4 and compatible generic effects. Each Raise adds +4 TN, with no Free Raises from training. Seal 1 Stone for 0-1 Raises; 2 for 2-3; 3 for 4-8. Failure leaves Stones Sealed.

4) Round & Turn

Each creature receives one Turn, normally 1 Movement, 1 Attack Action and 1 Reaction per Round. Movement and available Attack Actions can be used in either order. Activating an Active Buff during Preparation is free and does not consume an Attack Action. Reactions follow their printed trigger.

5) Power Use Limit

A named Power may be used once per Round, identified by its base Technical Reference across sources, PLs and delivery styles. Extra actions permit different legal Powers or Basic Attacks, not a repeat use of the same Power. Reactions with explicit repeat permission follow their text. Competing additional Attack Action grants use the highest single grant unless expressly stackable.

6) Initiative

At combat start, roll MR d8, keep all; 8s explode. Add Initiative modifiers. The resulting score persists across Rounds unless spent or changed by a rule.

7) Initiative Exchange

At Round start, before actions: apply first-round Initiative rolls, resolve any once-per-combat Initiative Boost, optionally convert Initiative to Initiative Colorless Stones at 4 × MR score per Stone, then lock turn order from remaining scores.

MR Initiative cost / Stone
2 8
3 12
4 16
5 20
6 24
7 28
8 32

Initiative stays at or above 0. Initiative Colorless Stones pay ordinary unlocked Stone costs and become Exhausted when used; recovery during combat requires Influence: Colorless Recovery. They disappear when combat ends and cannot be Sealed, Bound or burned.

Player Cheat Sheet: Defense & Resources

8) Attacks

  1. Choose the attack and legal targets; declare the number of Paid Raises and commit the number of Free Raises before rolling. Do not allocate them to Damage or Specials yet.
  2. Build the Pool and resolve one raised TN per target: Martial = effective Evade + 4 × Paid Raises; Spell = 4 × cast PL + effective SR + 4 × Paid Raises. AoE uses one roll against each target's TN.
  3. After the roll and hit checks, allocate the declared Raises to eligible Damage and/or an existing numeric Special once per Power use. Apply that selection to every successful hit, resolve eligible Special modifiers and Damage, then apply Armor and Damage Reduction.

Special value: printed + eligible after-roll allocated Special Raises + Stone Boost + eligible Passive Amplification + Vulnerability − Special Negation. There is no per-Round 4 × MR Special Application cap. A direct Spell below Base TN fizzles; otherwise each target compares its own Final TN. Other placed Spells use Creation TN as applicable. Persistent Special Zones and Special Auras apply automatically without rolls and cannot use Raises.

9) Damage

Damage dice explode only when their own rule allows it. Apply Armor, then combined Damage Reduction (max. 100%).

Final Damage = ceil(max(0, Damage − Effective Armor) × (1 − total DR/100))

If this yields zero, the natural-8 minimum still deals 1 damage per natural 8 on the original Damage Dice. Ongoing Special damage follows its own Armor rule.

10) Defense

Base Evade = MR × 4, modified by gear and effects. Direct creature-vs-creature struggles use Opposed Attribute Contests: both roll their relevant Attribute k MR, higher wins, ties preserve the current situation. The initiating side has Advantage and an unaware opponent has Disadvantage for the initial contest. Attribute Checks occur only when an effect calls for them: Vitality (body), Resolve (soul), Intellect (analysis), Wits (intrusion/senses). Their TN is printed or derived from Source MR/unranked danger as specified in Core.

11) Health & Fear

Health: Five normal Bars, each with Vitality × 4 boxes (Fortitude can raise that to ×5/×6/×7/×8 at PL 4/8/12/16). A fully marked Bar becomes Scarred. HP Healing refills an available Bar; Restoration reopens a Scarred Bar at full HP, including Broken to awaken an Incapacitated creature. Emergency Medicine: adjacent helper, 1 Attack Action, Base TN = patient MR × 4, success stabilizes; medical aftercare during Safe Haven Rest restores 2 Bars total with medical Profession Rank 4-7, 3 with medical Profession Rank 8, instead of the normal 1. Incapacitated characters cannot act or spend Stones; death follows the fiction, with reincarnation reserved for the GM Guide.

Fear: Roll Resolve k1 when called for: below 8: +2 Fear; 8–15: +1; 16+: +0. Each Fear removes one Attribute-Pool die before Health penalties; standard affected rolls retain at least 2 dice if the original Pool began at 2+. Fear is cleared by Safe Haven Rest.

12) Active Buffs

Maintain one Active Buff at a time. Activate or replace it freely during Preparation, including after Stone Confirmation, for no Attack Action or Stone cost; voluntary ending is possible at any time. Each activation lasts MR full Rounds, counting the activation Round. There is no general per-Combat activation limit, but spent individual per-Combat uses cannot be restored by replacing the Buff. Round-based Temporary HP/Damage Negation pools obey their printed refresh rules and cannot be duplicated by switching.

13) Stones

Start with 2 Attribute Stones. Earn 1 permanent Stone per 20 Lifetime XP; later Stones go to an Attribute (max MR × 2 per Attribute) or become Permanent Colorless at 1:1. Stone Abilities have 4 Ranks: normal cumulative costs 1/3/7/15; Premium 2/6/12/20.

Ready = available; Exhausted = spent until recovery; Sealed = returns after Safe Haven Rest; Bound = invested in a bond. At Round End, recover MR eligible Exhausted Stones total: Attribute Stones, plus Colorless Stones selected by Influence: Colorless Recovery. That Ability is prepared once per combat, and uses one shared MR recovery limit. At combat end, exhausted permanent Stones return and temporary Initiative Stones vanish. Sealed and Bound Stones follow their separate recovery rules.

14) Reroll Points

Maximum = Disadvantage Points. Refresh after Safe Haven Rest. Spend 1 to reroll your entire result or require the GM to reroll one roll; the new result stands.

15) Safe Haven Rest

Restore Reroll Points, Sealed Stones, eligible spent Stones and the available Health Bar; release Stone-Bound Form investments, return 1 Scarred Bar (qualified medical Profession aftercare: 2 or 3 total), and clear Fear.
